skill.name: dev-tools-skill
skill.description: Guides Chrome DevTools MCP debugging for frontend UI, console, network, and performance issues with step-by-step evidence collection and minimal fixes.
skill.summary: Debug live web app issues with Chrome DevTools MCP evidence and focused fix guidance.
skill.author: Eccentric-jamaican

security_audit.summary: All static findings were false positives caused by Markdown inline code for DevTools MCP tool names or benign debugging guidance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious automation instructions were found. The skill emphasizes evidence gathering, read-only inspection where possible, and confirmation before destructive actions.

static_findings.snippet: - `evaluate_script` -> read DOM/JS state (avoid mutations unless needed)
- Avoid forced synchronous layout in render loops
- Check console messages (`list_console_messages`, then `get_console_message` for details).
- Check network requests (`list_network_requests`, then `get_network_request` for errors/slow calls)
- Use `take_snapshot` to locate the target element; if unclear, `take_screenshot`.
- Inspect element text/attributes via `evaluate_script` (read-only DOM queries).
- If layout is involved, measure box sizes/positions via `evaluate_script`.
- Open failing request details (`get_network_request`), capture status, timing, payload.
- See `references/debug-workflows.md` for detailed steps and examples.
- Recommend fixes: reduce bundle size, defer non-critical JS, optimize images, avoid layout thrash.
- Avoid submitting forms or destructive actions without explicit user confirmation.

content.user_title: Debug Web Apps with Chrome DevTools
content.value_statement: Frontend bugs can be hard to reproduce from code alone. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Chrome DevTools MCP evidence gathering.
actual_capabilities: Selects Chrome pages and captures accessibility snapshots before diagnosis.
Reviews console messages and network requests for failures, slow calls, CORS, and payload issues.
Uses screenshots and read-only DOM queries to inspect UI layout, styles, and element state.
Runs performance traces and analyzes Core Web Vitals insights such as LCP, FCP, and CLS.
Suggests minimal CSS, JavaScript, API, or performance fixes with validation steps.
limitations: Requires a working Chrome DevTools MCP connection and an accessible target page.
Does not replace full browser automation tests or manual quality assurance.
May need user confirmation before form submission or destructive browser actions.
Cannot diagnose server-side defects unless browser evidence exposes the failure.

use_cases.title: Diagnose UI Interaction Bugs
use_cases.description: Inspect snapshots, screenshots, computed styles, and browser interactions to find layout or click problems.

use_cases.title: Investigate Failed Browser Flows
use_cases.description: Review console errors and network requests to identify failing endpoints, payload issues, or CORS problems.

use_cases.title: Triage Slow Web Pages
use_cases.description: Run performance traces, analyze top insights, and connect them to asset, script, or layout bottlenecks.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Basic UI Bug
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis for a visible page problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DevTools skill to inspect this page and explain why the button does not respond. Please describe each step in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Failed Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DevTools skill to review console and network evidence for this failed login flow. Find the first failing request and suggest a minimal fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Slow Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DevTools skill to run a performance trace with reload, identify the top insight, and connect it to network or layout evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Responsive Layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DevTools skill to compare desktop and mobile layouts, inspect computed styles, reproduce the interaction, and propose a reversible patch plan.

output_examples.input: My product page loads as a blank screen.
output_examples.output: The console shows the first app error during load. The likely cause is missing data before render. Suggested fix: guard the component state and validate with a reload.

output_examples.input: The landing page feels slow on first load.
output_examples.output: The trace points to slow LCP from a large hero image. Suggested fix: serve responsive image sizes and defer non-critical scripts.

output_examples.input: The dashboard login succeeds, but no data appears.
output_examples.output: The failing request returns an authorization error. Suggested fix: verify the auth header and token refresh path, then retest the flow.

best_practices: Start with a snapshot, console messages, and network requests before changing code.
Keep DOM scripts read-only unless the user approves a controlled mutation.
Summarize evidence, likely cause, smallest fix, and validation steps.
anti_patterns: Submitting forms or triggering destructive actions without explicit user confirmation.
Jumping to a code change before collecting browser evidence.
Running broad DOM mutations during diagnosis when observation is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill require Chrome DevTools MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for workflows where the Chrome DevTools MCP server can inspect a live page.

faq.question: Can it fix backend API bugs?
faq.answer: It can identify browser-visible API failures. Server-side root causes still require backend code or logs.

faq.question: Will it submit forms automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent to ask for confirmation before form submission or destructive actions.

faq.question: What evidence does it gather?
faq.answer: It gathers snapshots, screenshots, console messages, network request details, DOM state, and performance traces.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It tells the agent to explain actions in plain language and guide diagnosis step by step.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
